newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria could peg lev at present rate or higher.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria could peg lev at present rate or higher.

text.p: A currency board expected to be set up in Bulgaria early next year could be introduced at the current lev exchange rate or a higher lev rate, International Monetary Fund Resident Representative Franek Rozwadowski said.

"The information we have is that central bank foreign exchange and gold reserves are sufficient to set up a currency board at the current exchange rate or even a more appreciated one," Rozwadowski told a meeting of foreign businessmen.
The lev, which fell sharply against the dollar last week, closed on Friday at 361-365. It began last week at 272-275, but fell sharply as Bulgarians rushed to convert their savings to dollars.

A currency board is a form of fixed exchange rate regime which requires that levs in circulation and commercial banks' mimimum reserves at the central bank match central bank foreign exchange and gold reserves.
Currency boards have been used to restore confidence and bring inflation under control in other countries such as Argentina, Lithuania and Estonia.

Central bank reserves were $541 million at the end of October. The bank has gold reserves worth about $400 million and levs in circulation and commercial banks' minumum reserve deposits at the central bank total 180 billion levs.
The mechanism must be approved by parliament and is expected to be introduced in January or February.
Foreign debt payments of 300 million fall due in the first quarter of 1997, and the government has asked for additional financial help from the IMF and European Union.
The IMF may rebundle its existing $600 million standby accord, from which it has disbursed $120 million, but diplomats say there are no immediate plans for other funding.
